definitions.meaning: a bloomer here is something that blooms, a flowering plant, not a blunder
this climbing plant's trumpet flowers open at dawn and shut by afternoon

explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant whose blooms open with the dawn and fold up later in the day, so it both flowers and shuts early.

clue.text: Spy chief is found in inappropriate part

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
taken as written
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: The head of an intelligence agency turns up in an unsuitable role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is not 'discovered' here but the foundry verb, to cast.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor given an unsuitable role has been badly chosen for it.

clue.text: Stern military leader to provide new weapons

parts.note: the stern of a ship is its rear

indicators.note: the leader of the word military is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A strict general resolves to equip his troops again.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip again with arms is to give fresh weaponry.

clue.text: Beseech to bring one over from France

parts.note: to import goods is to bring them in
une is French for one, as said over the Channel

explanation.surface: A plea to ship a single item across from France.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to beg or pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Raising game can become such a habit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means reading it upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: brag is a card game similar to poker

explanation.surface: Lifting the stakes at cards can become a compulsive habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' is clothing, as a monk's habit, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit in the sense of dress or costume, as a nun's habit, is clothing.

clue.text: Loafer appears to knock fit sailor unconscious

parts.note: to lay someone low is to knock them down
AB stands for able-bodied seaman
out means out cold, unconscious

explanation.surface: An idler seems to knock a strong seaman out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is an idle person, a lazy good-for-nothing.

definitions.meaning: gardeners call a plant that differs from the standard type and is weeded out by this word
police keep photographs of criminals in this kind of gallery

explanation.definitionFit: Growers name an off-type seedling this way, and a criminal's photo hangs in the police's mugshot collection.

clue.text: Work over evangelist's official addition to epistle

indicators.note: over means the word for work is turned round

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
St Mark is one of the four evangelists, gospel writers

explanation.surface: A gospel writer's work handed over with an official note added to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Post Office stamps a date and place on each letter, an official mark added to mail.

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Handing out a gun to every individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given apiece is given to every individual separately.

indicators.note: the word for a role sits inside the word for dramatic

parts.note: stagy means theatrical, dramatic
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor's role in a theatrical farewell performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor's celebration on the eve of a wedding is his last fling of freedom.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the words for entering university are placed around the letter for right

parts.note: to go up is to enter a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student gets into college without being in the right social class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: GO UP is wrapped round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a set of things grouped together, a category.

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
mire is boggy ground, a swamp

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look up and notice a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is to respect and esteem them.

clue.text: Dispatched, in a working party to find missing person:- 3

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for dispatched goes inside the words for a working party

parts.note: a bee is a gathering of people working together, as in a sewing bee
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: Someone sent out with a search party to find a missing person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not present where expected is absent, a missing person.

definitions.meaning: builders say this when they lay the final, topmost stone of a structure
to stick up above the rest, rising out over the top

explanation.definitionFit: A builder's phrase for completing a structure by laying its last stone, and also for jutting above everything else.

clue.text: Top performer supports staff as a guiding principle

indicators.note: in a down clue the word below supports the word above, so the performer comes beneath the staff

parts.note: a staff is a pole
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A leading actor props up the cast as a principled guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Star guided navigators, so figuratively it is a fixed guide to conduct.

clue.text: Lay out money as means of gaining influence

definitions.meaning: to spend money on buying something
a firm grip or foothold giving leverage, as a climber's hold

explanation.definitionFit: To buy something is to spend money, and a grip or leverage is a hold giving advantage.

parts.note: a fly and a trap are both horse-drawn vehicles, not an insect-catching plant

explanation.definitionFit: A fly and a trap are both light horse-drawn vehicles for passengers.

clue.text: Part of speech to a boy, in other words? No

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
taken as written
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Telling a boy the word he spoke was a verb, then rejecting a paraphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating something word for word is the opposite of putting it in other words.

clue.text: Earth-god always takes in one adherent

indicators.note: the god and the word for always together surround the letter for one

parts.note: Bel was a Babylonian god of the earth
ever means always
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient earth god who forever welcomes a single follower.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent of a faith or cause is a follower who holds to it.

definitions.meaning: Veuve Clicquot, a French champagne whose name means widow Clicquot

explanation.definitionFit: Effervescent describes a lively person, and Veuve Clicquot, the widow, is a champagne, slangily called fizz.

definitions.meaning: someone who buys and sells shares on behalf of clients
broke means bankrupt, so this is its comparative, more broke

explanation.definitionFit: A dealer acting for investors, and also the comparative form of broke, meaning more penniless.

clue.text: Sort 'that' can' make street hard to go up

definitions.text: Sort 'that' can' make street hard to go up

parts.note: a street is a road
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word go is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A kind of person who makes a street hard to travel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish driver who hogs the middle of the carriageway is the type who obstructs traffic.

definitions.meaning: a small nocturnal African primate, the galago
children were traditionally told that babies were found under a gooseberry bush

explanation.walkthrough: British nursery lore tells children that new babies are found under a gooseberry bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A galago is a small African primate, and nursery lore says infants are found under gooseberry shrubs.

definitions.meaning: to grumble or complain, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A female canine, and slang for a complaint or a moan.

clue.text: Version of Maoism that is growing

indicators.note: a version of the word Maoism is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A new version of Chinese communist doctrine that is gaining ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia-like shrubs with yellow flowers are plants, things that grow.

clue.text: Part of tomahawk found in Nebraska

indicators.note: part of the word tomahawk holds the run of letters needed

explanation.surface: A piece of a Native American axe is unearthed in Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in that Midwestern US state.

annotationWithheld.why: Tart this king is passing round (4): FLAN is Tart, but no parse of 'this king is passing round' gives the letters or a second definition I can show

indicators.note: the word for advanced is to be said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: money advanced is lent

explanation.surface: Someone tended to come across as progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inclined is to lean or tilt, and this is the past tense.

indicators.note: edited suggests the letters have been reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor reworked the large page in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Telegraph is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a well-known British daily paper.

parts.note: London Cockneys replace a word with a phrase that chimes with it, a kind of verse-making freedom in everyday speech

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners, whose slang says 'apples and pears' for stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney speech swaps words for chiming phrases, like 'apples and pears' for stairs, a playful poetic device.
